```{r}
#| include = FALSE
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
template <- system.file("template", package = "rProject")
folders <- utils::read.delim(
  file = file.path(template, "folders.tsv"),
  colClasses = "character",
  quote = ""
)
```

Every project is an R project built from the rProject template:
a CRAN package, a manuscript, a library of references, a talk, or a
container image.
This vignette describes how such a project is laid out,
which files `make` writes,
and how a change travels from Overleaf to the public repository.
It is written for the user, for co-authors, and for AI agents.

## Types

The type is a line in `.setup/scripts/project.R`, for example
`type <- "cran"`.
Each type uses a few sets of template files
(`inst/template/<set>/`).

```{r}
#| echo = FALSE
sets <- rProject:::.TemplateSets()
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    type = names(sets),
    sets = vapply(
      X = sets,
      FUN = paste,
      FUN.VALUE = character(1),
      collapse = ", "
    ),
    use = c(
      "rProject itself",
      "R packages (cran-*, devel-*)",
      "manuscripts (man*), which are R packages too",
      "biblatex libraries (lib-*)",
      "talks",
      "container images (docker-*)"
    )
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Folders

The standard folders, the types that have them, and what they are for
(`inst/template/folders.tsv`).
Private folders stay on Overleaf and in the private repository;
they never go public.
`make` creates the folders marked "created" (with an empty `.gitignore`);
the others appear when they are needed.
`make tree` lists the folders of a project and flags the ones that are
missing or not standard for its type.

```{r}
#| echo = FALSE
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    folder = paste0("`", folders$folder, "`"),
    types = gsub(pattern = ",", replacement = ", ", x = folders$types),
    private = ifelse(as.logical(folders$private), "yes", ""),
    created = ifelse(as.logical(folders$create), "yes", ""),
    purpose = folders$purpose
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

Notes:

- `.setup/notes/` is private.
  Library projects keep the reference PDFs there.
- `.setup/bin/` is optional:
  `Binary()` runs its R scripts at `make project`
  (for example, to build a bespoke binary).
- Code coverage: to leave files out, put covr's `.covrignore` at the
  project root and add it to `.Rbuildignore`
  (`ignore` in `.setup/scripts/project.R`).
- The naming rules for files in `R/`, `tests/testthat/`,
  `.setup/r-dependencies/`, and the test folders are in the R style guide
  (`.setup/latex/rProject-002-style-R.Rtex`).

## Template files

`rProject::Template()` (run by `make project` and `make template`)
keeps the template files of a project in step with rProject.
Each file has a tier:

- **Tier 1, links.** Files that Overleaf or `make` needs
  (`Makefile`, `latexmkrc`, the LaTeX preamble, ...).
  They are linked into the Overleaf project from rProject's Overleaf
  project.
  `Template()` never writes them; it lists those that differ as links to
  refresh.
- **Tier 2, written by `make`.** Everything else: the workflows,
  the make scripts, the Quarto pages, the folder skeleton.
  `Template()` writes a file that is missing or differs
  (the template wins: change it in rProject).
  These files are not uploaded to Overleaf.

Workflows that only some projects run are in a catalog
(`inst/template/workflows/`).
A project names the ones it runs in `project.R`:

```r
workflows <- c("docker-build-push-multi", "docker-build-push-daily-multi")
workflow_daily <- "docs"
workflow_title <- "Docker Build and Push Docs [multi] (Daily)"
workflow_cron <- "30 3 * * *"
```

The daily docker workflow is written as
`docker-build-push-daily-multi-<workflow_daily>.yml`,
with its title and cron filled in.

Files that leave the template are listed in
`inst/template/removed.tsv`.
`Template()` deletes them (a folder only when nothing but `.gitignore`
files is left in it) and names them, so that they can be deleted in
Overleaf too.

```{r}
#| echo = FALSE
removed <- utils::read.delim(
  file = file.path(template, "removed.tsv"),
  colClasses = "character"
)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    path = paste0("`", removed$path, "`"),
    since = removed$since
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## From Overleaf to the public repository

1. **Edit on Overleaf.**
   Overleaf is the main editor.
   Co-authors edit there.
   Agents edit a local clone; the user uploads the changed files.
2. **Log.**
   Every change set (one Overleaf push) has a log in
   `.setup/logs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md` (`make log`),
   with the commit message and the files to upload or delete.
3. **O2G.**
   The user pushes from Overleaf to the private GitHub repository.
   `make verify RECORD=TRUE` checks that the private repository matches
   the local clone and records the push in the log and in
   `.setup/logs/index.md`.
4. **PUB.**
   `make all` builds and checks everything;
   `make auto` checks the public export
   (no private files, nothing over 50 MB, no tokens)
   and pushes to the public repository.

## Make targets

| Target | Does |
|---|---|
| `make project` | settings, template files, AI files |
| `make all` | build, docs, LaTeX, pkgdown, Quarto, coverage |
| `make lint` | style and lint the R code; report Overleaf limits |
| `make sizecheck` | check Overleaf limits |
| `make spec TOPIC=<topic>` | start a spec for a change set |
| `make log TOPIC=<topic> SUMMARY="..."` | write the change-set log |
| `make verify RECORD=TRUE` | verify and record a push from Overleaf |
| `make auto` | publish to the public repository |
| `make tree` | the project's folders and what each is for |
| `make template` | write the template files only |
| `make latex`, `make pdf` | knit and compile the LaTeX sources |

R runs only inside an Apptainer image:
`apptainer exec <image> make <target>`.

## Keywords

Short messages from the user to an AI agent:

| Keyword | Means |
|---|---|
| "O2G" | the user pushed from Overleaf to GitHub: verify and record the push |
| "PUB" | the user ran `make all` and `make auto`: check the public repository and its CI |
| "build docs" | publish the docker images in order and rebuild the `docs` images |
| "EX" | the user is leaving: update `.setup/notes/claude.txt` and the handoff |
| "handoff" | rewrite `.setup/ai/handoff.md` without leaving |

The private files that agents read (`AGENTS.md`, `.setup/ai/`) are
written by `rProject::AI()`.
